_why: ADR 0095's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
check_documented_counts.py grew an ADR-count matcher and applied it to
every present-tense contributor document except README.md, which it
skipped as 'already checked above, in more detail'. The detailed check
covered test counts, domain counts and guard counts and never covered
ADRs. README.md:449 said '23 decision records' while docs/adr/ held 93.
The matcher was never broken. --selftest asserts it catches the exact
string '`docs/adr/` — 23 decision records' and had been passing the
whole time. The guard proved it could find that sentence and was never
pointed at the file containing it.
W3, W4 and W5 are the rows that matter. --write is a script that edits
the README, so the tests worth having are the ones proving what it
REFUSES to touch: the domain count (a judgment call the guard
deliberately does not derive), a quoted example (evidence, not a
claim), and an approximate figure inside its tolerance. A --write that
rewrote any of those would make a guess look verified, which is worse

mutations.description: the README is exempted from the ADR rule again
mutations._note: The defect itself. adr_failures returning nothing for README is how '23 decision records' outlived seventy ADRs.
mutations.find:
failures: List[str] = []
    for lineno, claimed in documented_adr_counts(text):

mutations.description: the ADR tolerance widens far enough to swallow the real gap
mutations._note: 23 against 93 is a gap of 70. A guard whose tolerance is wide enough to accept it is reporting on nothing, and a tolerance is the easiest thing in a check to loosen without noticing.
mutations.find:
tolerance = 3 if approximate else 0
        if abs(value - actual) > tolerance:
mutations.replace:
tolerance = 300 if approximate else 300
        if abs(value - actual) > tolerance:

mutations._note: The count the guard refuses to derive, because DISPATCH includes a run-mode and a generic ingest path that are not teaching domains. Automating it would bury a judgment call inside a script and present the result as measured.
mutations.find:
text = apply(
        text, re.compile(r"(~)?\s*(\d+) guard scripts?\b", re.IGNORECASE),
        guards, "guard scripts",
    )
mutations.replace:
text = apply(
        text, re.compile(r"(~)?\s*(\d+) guard scripts?\b", re.IGNORECASE),
        guards, "guard scripts",
    )
    text = apply(
        text, re.compile(r"(~)?\s*(\d+) simulation domains\b", re.IGNORECASE),
        guards, "domains",
    )

mutations.description: --write corrects quoted examples along with real claims
mutations._note: docs/README.md explains an exclusion by quoting a stale figure. Rewriting the quotation edits the evidence to match the claim -- the failure mode this whole project exists to find, performed by a tool.
mutations.find: if abs(was - value) <= tolerance or is_quoted(_l, m.start(), m.end()):

mutations.description: --write sharpens an approximate figure inside its tolerance
mutations._note: `~60 guard scripts` becoming `~62` converts a deliberately loose statement into a false-precise one, and teaches writers that hedging buys nothing.

mutations.description: --write writes a test count from an incomplete collection
mutations._note: The rule that matters. An invented number a tool has just written reads as freshly verified, which is strictly worse than a stale one. The first version of this test drove it through main() by stubbing collect_count, and the branch turned out to be unreachable -- with no test counts to compare there were no failures, so --write was never entered. The rule was moved into rewrite(), where it belongs, and the wholesale refusal was deleted: guard and ADR counts come from file globs and have nothing to do with whether pytest can collect.

mutations.description: --write drops thousands separators from the tree diagram
mutations._note: `1,141` becoming `1141` shifts an aligned column and puts a formatting diff in every PR that adds a test. A fixer that makes a mess is a fixer nobody runs.
mutations.find: shown = f"{value:,}" if "," in m.group(2) else str(value)

mutations._note: A second run finding more to change means the first run's output was not stable, and `make counts-fix; make guards` would still fail.
mutations.find:
if abs(was - value) <= tolerance or is_quoted(_l, m.start(), m.end()):
                    return m.group(0)
